label: First edition printed Chapter CIV life prorogator heading and day/night luminary prerequisite across seam
claims: heading
CHAP CIV prorogator Life Hylech Hyleg Apheta
A separate chapter introduces Hylech/Hyleg/Apheta as the alleged prorogator of life and an interficient/killing planet.
Printed CIV/editorial CV, separate from infant-survival chapter above page561 divider.
definition
word Chaldean planet or place heaven
Lilly describes Hylech as a Chaldean term for a planet or place of Heaven.
Period astrological terminology, not medical prognostic variable.
definition
which being directed judge Life estate thereof
A selected planet or point's direction is claimed to determine life or its state.
No verified individual time-of-death or survival outcome.
method
Hylech thus found in Diurnall take Sun, Nocturnall Moon
The first branch starts with Sun for daytime and Moon for nighttime births.
The rule crosses PDF561–562; one conditional branch, not two unrelated predictions.

label: Eligible Hylegical positions and fallback Moon, preceding syzygy and ascending degree
claims: condition
convenient Hylegiacall places houses first tenth eleventh seventh ninth
Sun or Moon can be accepted as Hyleg only in the first, tenth, eleventh, seventh or ninth houses or their stated orbs.
House-set admissibility is source critical.
condition
within Orbs houses
The eligiblity extends to planets within house orbs.
Exact numerical house orb not supplied here.
condition
space Equator under earth rejected
Sun/Moon below the horizon are rejected as candidate Hyleg under the general rule.
Source gives an explicit Ascendant-near exception.
exception
unless within twenty five degrees ascendant
A planet below Earth within 25 degrees of Ascendant is an exception.
Specific 25-degree angular threshold must be preserved.
condition
eighth house and twelfth rejected
Sun or Moon positioned in eighth or twelfth house is rejected as a Hyleg candidate.
Another hard source prohibition.
method
if Sun not capable then Moon
In the default preference order, if Sun's position disqualifies it Lilly checks the Moon.
Preserve ordered fallback rather than selecting Moon freely.
method
if neither consider if geniture diurnall new Moon precede
If neither luminary qualifies and birth is diurnal, inspect preceding new Moon.
Source branch refers to event before birth.
method
nocturnal observe full Moon going before Birth
In night births the preceding full Moon is considered.
Separate from diurnal new-Moon branch.
method
Planet hath most dominion these places
He asks which planet rules the chosen syzygy degree via essential dignities.
Requires historical dignity scores and epoch data.
condition
least three essential fortitudes
The dignity candidate must possess at least three essential fortitudes at selected place.
Source threshold; not independent outcome correlation.
condition
Planet in Hylegiacall house
The selected dignity-holder must also lie in an eligible Hylegical house.
An essential conjunct condition, not optional.
method
if not apt house simply let Horoscope be Hyleg
If strongest dignity-holder is not in an eligible house, use the Ascendant as Hyleg.
Ordered fallback, do not discard.
historical_alternative
some Artists ever use Ascendant
Lilly acknowledges that some astrologers always take Ascendant as Hyleg and reject other methods.
Competing historical choice, not corroborating result.
exception
diurnall ever regard degree New Moon preceding though full intervened
For a day birth he says to consider the earlier new-Moon degree even if a full Moon intervened shortly before birth.
Could conflict with simpler last-syzygy reading; preserve exact qualification.
authorial_rationale
by day Sun more powerful than Moon
He explains this diurnal preference through Sun's claimed greater power.
Not scientifically demonstrated.
method
nocturnal consider Moon at Birth
In a night chart one candidate position is Moon's degree at birth.
First of three night candidate positions.
method
nocturnal place Opposition or full Moon preceding
Night-chart candidates include preceding full-Moon/opposition degree.
Second candidate; historical syzygy calculation unverified.
method
nocturnal Part of Fortune at Birth
The natal Part of Fortune is another candidate at night.
Third candidate; derived figure dependent on sect and chart calculations.

label: Hyleg candidate selection, comparative luminaries, unresolved method and opening Anareta position
claims: condition
if such a Planet in Aphetical place he shall be Prorogator
The strongest candidate planet is appointed the life prorogator if it occupies an eligible Aphetical position.
Candidate conditions inherited from previous page.
method
if not so new Moon preceded take Ascendant
If the dignity planet is not suitably placed and a new Moon preceded, Lilly takes the Ascendant.
Fallback branch.
method
if full Moon ... take Part Fortune if Aphetical else Ascendant
After a preceding full Moon, use Part of Fortune if eligible, otherwise Ascendant.
Source distinctly uses Part of Fortune versus Ascendant.
exception
in nocturnal Births care to full Moon though conjunction next
In night births he says the preceding full Moon may still matter even if a new Moon follows near the birth.
Source allows looking past the immediately preceding phase.
definition
Luminary place degree where Light above earth
The source defines relevant luminary position in terms of the light being above the horizon at the syzygy.
May require specialized historic day/night syzygy context.
condition
both Lights ... Planet Governor proper place all Aphetical
He also considers a case where both luminaries and a ruling planet occupy eligible life-significator places.
Multi-candidate comparison.
method
place Light preferred greater virtue more apt place
Choose the light judged stronger in dignities and more suitable house placement.
No fixed universally applied numerical score specified here.
example
nocturnal Moon ninth or seventh Sun Ascendant prefer Sun
In a night chart, Sun in Ascendant may be preferred over Moon in ninth/seventh.
Example overrides naive automatic sect-first selection.
condition
Sun nearer ascending or dignified within25 degrees
That preference strengthens if Sun is close to rising degree, essentially dignified or within 25° of Ascendant.
Source explicit conditional.
example
diurnal Moon tenth Sun ninth prefer Moon
In a day chart Moon in tenth may outrank Sun in ninth.
Another counterexample to always choosing the sect luminary.
example
Moon tenth Sun eleventh seem equal
Moon in tenth and Sun in eleventh are described as roughly equal eligibility.
Requires tie resolution.
method
break tie most essential or accidental dignities
To resolve comparable lights select one with greatest essential or accidental dignities.
Different from first fallback.
method
if equal see disposer applying good aspect
If still tied, examine whether a dispositor applies to either luminary favorably.
Adds further choice.
condition
potent dispositor favourable aspect strengthens Hyleg
A strong dispositor aspecting candidate Hyleg favorably is said to make the life significator stronger.
Astrological assertion, not empirical survival proof.
authorial_negative
I rest not satisfied how take Hyleg aright
Lilly expressly says he remains unsatisfied about the correct way of selecting a Hyleg.
Major uncertainty: do not present procedure as reliably solved by its author.
authorial_negative
whom properly Killing Interficient Destroying Planet Anareta
He also says he is uncertain which planet should properly count as the killing/Anareta planet.
The source admits definitional and selection ambiguity.
historical_attribution
Ancients Anareta in eighth house
He reports an ancient proposal that the Anareta be found in eighth house.
A theory from earlier practitioners, not his experimentally validated result.
condition
five degrees before cusp eighth or twenty five after
The cited Anareta definition extends from five degrees before the eighth cusp to twenty-five degrees afterward.
Specific 5°/25° window; verify use of cusp direction and orientation.
